title: Project intake
intro:
A few questions so the next step can be planned properly.

Nothing here is mandatory. **Skip** anything that does not apply, and say *I don't know* wherever that is the honest answer — both are useful, and neither stops you from handing the result back.
impact: decides whether the work is scoped as an adaptation or as something new

sections.title: Scope
sections.intro: What the work has to cover, and what it must leave alone.

questions.question: Is there an existing system this has to fit into?
questions.why: decides whether we design freely or adapt to something that already exists
questions.context: An *existing system* is anything already in use that this work cannot simply replace — a running service, a spreadsheet everyone relies on, a process people have learned.

options.label: Yes, and it must not change
Yes, but parts of it can be adapted

questions.question: Which parts of it must keep working exactly as they do now?
questions.why: these become the constraints everything else is designed around
questions.detail: Name the components, screens or reports people depend on. If you are not sure, name the ones that would cause the loudest complaints if they broke.

questions.question: Is there a budget ceiling we should design against?
questions.why: an honest ceiling is worth more than a generous estimate

questions.question: Which of these matter most?
questions.why: when two of them collide, this says which one wins
questions.context: Pick as many as genuinely apply — but if everything matters, nothing does.

options.label: Covering every case from the start
Being able to hand it over to someone else later
